column2: On the authority of Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the grandson of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his sweet basil (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said:
I memorised from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Leave what gives you doubt for what does not give you doubt.” Reported by al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī; al-Tirmidhī said: “A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.”

This hadith contains the command to leave whatever a person has doubts about, which his soul is not at ease with and which stirs unease and disquiet in it, and to turn to what his heart is comfortable with and his soul is at ease with.

This hadith resembles what came earlier in the hadith of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr: “Whoever guards against the doubtful matters has kept his religion and his honour free of blame, and whoever falls into the doubtful matters falls into the unlawful.”
Both show that a God-fearing person should not consume wealth in which there is doubt, just as consuming what is unlawful is forbidden to him.
Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (1/280): “The meaning of this hadith goes back to stopping at doubtful matters and guarding against them,

for what is purely lawful does not cause any doubt (rayb) in the believer's heart—rayb meaning unease and disquiet—rather, the soul rests in it and the heart is at ease with it. As for doubtful matters, they cause the hearts unease and disquiet that bring about uncertainty.”
He also said (1/283): “There is a matter here that one should be alert to: being meticulous in holding back from doubtful matters befits only someone whose affairs are all upright
and whose deeds are consistently marked by taqwā and scrupulousness. As for someone who openly violates what is plainly unlawful and then wants to be scrupulous about some subtle doubtful matter,
that is not to be tolerated from him; rather, it is to be censured, as Ibn ʿUmar said to someone from the people of Iraq who asked him about the blood of mosquitoes:
‘They ask me about the blood of mosquitoes when they have killed al-Ḥusayn, and I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “They [al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn] are my two sweet basils of this world.”’”
One should leave what involves doubt and take what involves none.
Leaving what one has doubts about brings the soul rest and keeps it safe from unease.
